# Nehemiah Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 472r–472v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_009_page_001.jpg

---

**1** On the twenty-fourth day of the month, the Israelites came together again — this time fasting, wearing rough sackcloth, and with dust on their heads as signs of grief.

**2** Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all foreigners. They stood before God and openly confessed their sins and the sins of their ancestors.

**3** They spent a quarter of the day standing in their places as the Book of the Law of the LORD their God was read aloud, and another quarter confessing and worshiping the LORD.

**4** Standing on the Levites' platform, Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani called out to the LORD their God with loud voices.

**5** Then the Levites — Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah — said, "Stand up and praise the LORD your God, who lives from everlasting to everlasting!" Then they prayed:

"May your glorious name be praised — it is far beyond all that any blessing or praise can express.

**6** You alone are the LORD. You created the heavens — even the highest heavens — with all their starry host. You made the earth and everything on it, the seas and all they contain. You give life to everything, and the heavenly beings worship you.

**7** You are the LORD God, the one who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur in Babylonia, and renamed him Abraham.

**8** You found him faithful, and you made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites to his descendants. And you have kept that promise, because you are righteous.

**9** You saw how our ancestors suffered in Egypt. You heard their desperate cries at the Red Sea.

**10** You performed miraculous signs and wonders against Pharaoh, his officials, and all his people, because you knew how cruelly they had treated our ancestors. You won an enduring reputation for yourself that stands to this very day.

**11** You split the sea open so our ancestors could walk through on dry ground. Their enemies, who were chasing them, you hurled into the depths — like stones sinking into a raging sea.

**12** By day you guided them with a pillar of cloud, and by night with a pillar of fire, lighting the path they needed to follow.

**13** You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven. You gave them fair laws, reliable teachings, and good commandments and statutes.

**14** You revealed your holy Sabbath to them and delivered your commands, statutes, and instructions through your servant Moses.

**15** When they were hungry, you gave them bread from the sky. When they were thirsty, you brought water streaming from a rock. You told them to go and take possession of the land you had promised them.

**16** But our ancestors became arrogant. They became stubborn and refused to follow your commands.

**17** They refused to listen. They forgot the miracles you had done for them. They dug in their heels and even chose a leader to take them back to slavery in Egypt! But you — you are a God who forgives. You are gracious and compassionate, patient and overflowing with faithful love. You did not abandon them.

**18** Even when they cast an idol in the shape of a calf and declared, 'This is your god who rescued you from Egypt!' — even when they committed such outrageous blasphemy —

**19** you, in your boundless compassion, still did not abandon them in the wilderness. The cloud continued to guide them by day, the fire continued to light their way by night.

**20** You sent your good Spirit to teach them. You continued feeding them manna and giving them water for their thirst.

**21** For forty years you provided for them in the wilderness. They had everything they needed. Their clothes never wore out; their feet never swelled.

**22** You handed over kingdoms and nations to them, parceling out even the remotest territories. They conquered the land of King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan.

**23** You multiplied their descendants until they were as numerous as the stars in the sky, and you brought them into the land you had promised their ancestors.

**24** Their children entered and conquered the land. You crushed the Canaanites before them and handed over their kings and peoples to do with as they pleased.

**25** They captured fortified cities and rich farmland. They took over houses stocked with goods, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and orchards everywhere. They ate until they were full. They grew prosperous and reveled in your extraordinary generosity.

**26** Yet despite all this, they rebelled against you. They threw your Law over their shoulder and ignored it. They murdered the prophets you sent to call them back. They committed one outrage after another.

**27** So you handed them over to their enemies, who crushed them. But when they cried out to you in their suffering, you heard them from heaven and — true to your boundless compassion — you sent deliverers who rescued them.

**28** Yet as soon as they had peace, they went right back to doing evil. So you gave them over to their enemies again. But when they cried out once more, you heard from heaven and rescued them — again and again, because of your great compassion.

**29** You warned them to return to your Law, but they arrogantly refused. They violated your commands — the very commands that give life to anyone who follows them. They stubbornly turned away and refused to listen.

**30** Year after year you patiently bore with them. You sent your Spirit through the prophets to warn them. But they would not listen. Finally, you allowed the surrounding nations to conquer them.

**31** But even then, your compassion was so great that you did not destroy them completely or abandon them forever — because you are a gracious and merciful God.

**32** And so now, our God — the great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God who faithfully keeps every covenant promise — please do not regard lightly all the suffering that has overwhelmed us: our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all your people, from the days of the Assyrian kings until today.

**33** In everything that has happened to us, you have been just. You have acted faithfully; we are the ones who did wrong.

**34** Our kings, leaders, priests, and ancestors did not follow your Law. They ignored your commands and the warnings you gave them.

**35** Even while they had their own kingdom — enjoying the abundant goodness you lavished on them in the spacious, fertile land you provided — they refused to serve you and would not turn from their evil ways.

**36** And so here we are today — slaves! Slaves in the very land you gave our ancestors to enjoy! We live on it, but its bounty belongs to others.

**37** The land's rich harvests go to the kings you have placed over us because of our sins. They do whatever they want with our bodies and our livestock. We are in terrible distress."

**38** In light of all this, we are making a binding agreement and putting it in writing. Our leaders, Levites, and priests have sealed it with their names.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes
1. **Israel's story as God's story** — This prayer is one of the longest continuous theological narratives in Scripture, retelling Israel's history from Abraham to the present. But the real subject is not Israel — it is God's character: faithful, forgiving, patient, merciful. Israel's failures are the dark backdrop against which God's steadfast love shines.
2. **The cycle of grace** — The prayer reveals a devastating pattern: blessing leads to disobedience, which leads to judgment, which leads to crying out, which leads to deliverance — repeated "many times" (v. 28). Yet God never breaks the cycle from his side; only Israel breaks it from theirs.
3. **"We are slaves this day" (v. 36)** — The prayer's most searing line. The Exodus — God's defining act — appears reversed: they are in the Promised Land, yet they are enslaved. This theological paradox is the foundation for the covenant renewal that follows.

*— PNEUMA*
